questions.question: The art of decoration, called Pietra dura became popular during whose reign?
questions.solution:
• Art: Shah Jahan
  • Architecture: Pietra Dura involves inlaying cut, polished, colored stones into marble to create images.

questions.question: "India House", a revolutionary organisation, was established by Shyamji Krishna Varma in ________ for the spread of Indian Nationalism.
questions.solution:
• Revolutionary: London
  • Shyamji: India House served as a hub for revolutionaries like Savarkar and Hardayal in the UK.

questions.question: Who was the president of the second session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
• President: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • INC: The 1886 Calcutta Session saw the merging of the National Congress and National Conference.

questions.question: Who among the following was defeated by Mauryan emperor Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
• Defeat: Seleucus Nicator
  • Conflict: Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus and gained the territories of Arachosia and Gedrosia.

questions.question: Sabha and Ur, two kinds of village assemblies are referred to in which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
• Assemblies: Chola
  • Local Govt: The Cholas are most famous for their highly organized village self-government systems.

questions.question: Elphinstone was the Governor of which province of India during 1819-27?
questions.solution:
• Province: Bombay
  • Mountstuart Elphinstone: He was a pioneer in state education in India and the first Governor of Bombay.

questions.question: The Cabinet Mission came to India in ________ to discuss the ultimate transfer of power.
questions.solution:
• Mission: 1946
  • Plan: The Cabinet Mission proposed a federal structure for India to prevent partition.

questions.question: When was the first Session of the Lok Sabha of independent India held?
questions.solution:
• Session: 13th May 1952
  • Parliament: This marked the beginning of the First Lok Sabha after the first general elections.

questions.question: Who among the following signed the Poona pact with Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
• Pact: Bhimrao Ambedkar
  • Result: The Poona Pact (1932) gave reserved seats to the Depressed Classes instead of separate electorates.

questions.question: Under whose reign was the maximum number of books in Persian on classical Indian Music written?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Aurangzeb
  • Music: Although he banned music in court, more Persian books on Indian music were written during his reign than any other.

questions.question: Who among the following was the most famous Shaka ruler, who got the Sudarshana Lake in Kathiawar renovated?
questions.solution:
• Shaka Ruler: Rudradaman I
  • Inscription: The Junagadh Inscription is the first long inscription ever recorded in chaste Sanskrit.

questions.question: The local communities of merchants were known as ________ in the Vijayanagara empire.
questions.solution:
• Merchants: Kudirai Chettis
  • Trade: Horse merchants were vital for the Vijayanagara army to maintain a strong cavalry against northern Sultanates.

questions.question: Who wrote the Mauryan period book Arthashastra?
questions.solution:
• Author: Vishnu Gupta
  • Mauryan: Better known as Chanakya, his Arthashastra covers military strategy, economics, and politics.

questions.question: The first railway line in India was started from _____ to ______ in 1853.
questions.solution:
• Railway: Bombay to Thane
  • Start: The first train ran a distance of 34 km with 400 guests on 16th April 1853.

questions.question: Through which of the following organisations did Annie Besant promote the studies of ancient Indian religions, philosophies and doctrines?
questions.solution:
• Organization: Theosophical Society
  • Annie Besant: She joined in 1889 and moved to India in 1893 to head the society in Adyar.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders from INC attended the Second Round Table Conference?
questions.solution:
• Conference: Mahatma Gandhi
  • 1931: Gandhi was the sole representative of the INC at the Second Round Table Conference in London.

questions.question: Self-Government or ‘Swaraj’ as the ultimate goal of the Indian National Congress—this declaration was made by Dadabhai Naoroji in which of the following sessions of the INC?
questions.solution:
• Slogan: Calcutta
  • 1906: Under Naoroji, the Congress first used the word 'Swaraj' as its political goal.

questions.question: The Vakataka dynasty was directly related to which Gupta emperor?
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Chandra Gupta II
  • Alliance: He married his daughter Prabhavatigupta into the Vakataka family to secure his southern borders.

questions.question: Where did Vivekananda participate at the World’s Parliament of Religions?
questions.solution:
• Location: Chicago
  • Vivekananda: His speech beginning with 'Sisters and brothers of America' made him a global figure in 1893.

questions.question: Krishnadeva Raya composed a work on ____________ in Telugu known as the Amuktamalyada.
questions.solution:
• Work: statecraft
  • Krishnadeva Raya: Amuktamalyada is an epic poem in Telugu that also details the King's duties.

questions.question: Who among the following gave the famous ‘Do or Die’ slogan during Quit India Movement?
questions.solution:
• Slogan: Mahatma Gandhi
  • 1942: The 'Do or Die' speech was delivered at the start of the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: During the reign of Akbar, _______ was the land that has lain fallow for three or four years.
questions.solution:
• Land: Chachar
  • Revenue: Under the Dahsala System, land was classified based on how often it was cropped.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters lost his life during the protest against Simon Commission where black flags were waved at the Commission?
questions.solution:
• Martyr: Lala Lajpat Rai
  • Simon Commission: Known as 'Sher-e-Punjab', he died weeks after being injured in the protest.

questions.question: Kosala Mahajanapada (6th century BCE) is a part of modern day:
questions.solution:
• Location: Uttar Pradesh
  • Mahajanapada: Kosala included the holy city of Ayodhya and was a major power in the 6th century BCE.

questions.question: Where was the first All India Kisan Sabha formed?
questions.solution:
• Peasants: Lucknow
  • 1936: Sahajanand Saraswati was the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha.

questions.question: Who was the first nationalist to give the theory of drain of wealth from India to England?
questions.solution:
• Theorist: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • Economic: He argued that £12 million was drained from India to England every year.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to qualify for Covenanted service?
questions.solution:
• First Indian: Satyendra Nath Tagore
  • ICS: The elder brother of Rabindranath Tagore, he joined the Civil Services in 1863.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first non-European to win a Noble prize in 1913 in literature for his work ‘Gitanjali’?
questions.solution:
• Winner: Rabindranath Tagore
  • Literature: He was the first Asian to receive a Nobel Prize for his collection of poems.

questions.question: _________ was the chairman of the planning commission when the first five year plan was formulated in India.
questions.solution:
• Chairman: Jawaharlal Nehru
  • Planning: The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) was based on the Harrod-Domar model.

questions.question: In 1942, the British government sent the ________ mission to India.
questions.solution:
• Mission: Cripps
  • 1942: Stafford Cripps promised 'Dominion Status' after the war, which Gandhi called a 'post-dated cheque.'
